passages.text: DataKit is a lightweight Python library for tabular data processing. Install it with: pip install datakit. The minimum supported Python version is 3.10.
DataKit is a lightweight Python library for tabular data processing. Install it with: pip install datakit. The minimum supported Python version is 3.8.
Use datakit.load_csv(path) to load a CSV file into a DataKit Table. The function returns a Table object. Encoding defaults to UTF-8.
datakit.load_json(path) loads a JSON array of objects into a Table. Nested objects are flattened using dot notation for column names.
datakit.load_parquet(path) loads a Parquet file. Parquet support requires the optional dependency pyarrow: pip install datakit[parquet].
A DataKit Table has attributes .columns (list of column names) and .shape (rows, cols). Call table.head(n=5) to preview the first n rows.
Filter rows with table.filter(predicate). The predicate is a callable that receives a row dict and returns True to keep the row.
Select columns with table.select(['col_a', 'col_b']). Drop columns with table.drop(['col_c']). Both return a new Table.
Sort a table with table.sort_by('column', ascending=True). Missing values are placed at the end by default.
Aggregate with table.groupby('key').agg({'value': 'sum'}). Supported aggregations are sum, mean, count, min, and max.
Aggregate with table.groupby('key').agg({'value': 'sum'}). Supported aggregations are sum, mean, and count only.
table.describe() returns summary statistics for every numeric column: count, mean, std, min, 25%, 50%, 75%, and max.
Join two tables with table.join(other, on='key', how='inner'). Supported join types are inner, left, right, and outer.
Join two tables with table.join(other, on='key', how='inner'). Only inner and left joins are supported.
Handle missing values with table.fill_na(value) or table.dropna(how='any'). fill_na replaces nulls; dropna removes rows with nulls.
Detect missing values with table.isna() which returns a Table of booleans, or table.null_count() which returns a dict of column to null count.
Export a Table with table.to_csv(path), table.to_json(path), or table.to_parquet(path). to_parquet requires pyarrow.
table.to_dict(orient='records') returns a list of row dicts. orient='list' returns a dict of column name to value list.
Cast column types with table.astype({'age': 'int', 'score': 'float'}). Supported types are int, float, str, bool, and datetime.
Parse dates with table.parse_dates(['created_at']). The default date format is ISO 8601. Pass format= to override.
Global options are set via datakit.set_option(name, value). Available options: display.max_rows (default 20) and display.precision (default 6).
Global options are set via datakit.set_option(name, value). Available options: display.max_rows (default 10) and display.precision (default 4).
Reset all options to defaults with datakit.reset_options(). Read the current value with datakit.get_option(name).
DataKit ships a CLI: datakit preview file.csv prints the first 10 rows. datakit info file.csv prints shape and column dtypes.
Convert formats from the CLI: datakit convert input.csv output.parquet. Supported conversions: csv, json, parquet.
For tables larger than 1 million rows, enable streaming mode with datakit.load_csv(path, streaming=True). Streaming mode processes chunks of 10_000 rows.
table.lazy() returns a LazyTable that defers computation until .collect() is called. Chained filters and selects are fused into a single pass.
DataKit raises ColumnNotFoundError when a requested column is missing. SchemaError is raised on type cast failures. FileFormatError is raised for unsupported file types.
All DataKit exceptions inherit from datakit.DataKitError. Catch DataKitError to handle any library-specific failure.
DataKit is released under the MIT License. The source repository is hosted at https://github.com/example/datakit.
The current stable release of DataKit is 2.1.0. Check the installed version with: import datakit; print(datakit.__version__).
The current stable release of DataKit is 1.4.2. Check the installed version with: import datakit; print(datakit.__version__).
Apply a function to each row with table.apply(fn, axis='rows') or to each column with axis='columns'. The function must return a single value per row or column.
Concatenate tables vertically with datakit.concat([t1, t2]). Columns are aligned by name; missing columns are filled with null.
Sample rows with table.sample(n=100, seed=42) for a fixed-size sample, or table.sample(frac=0.1) for a fraction of rows.
Set an index column with table.set_index('id'). Reset with table.reset_index(). Indexed lookups use table.loc[key].
Basic plotting is available via table.plot(kind='hist', column='age'). Supported kinds are hist, bar, line, and scatter. Matplotlib is an optional dependency.
Validate a schema with table.validate(schema) where schema is a dict of column to expected type. Returns True on success or raises SchemaError.
Chain transformations with table.pipe(fn1).pipe(fn2). Each function receives a Table and returns a Table. Useful for reusable pipelines.
Run SQL against a Table with datakit.sql(table, 'SELECT name, age FROM t WHERE age > 30'). The table is registered as alias t.
The weather in Reykjavik averages 5 degrees Celsius in summer. Pack a warm jacket if you visit Iceland.
A standard chessboard has 64 squares arranged in an 8 by 8 grid. Each player starts with 16 pieces.
Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy in plants. Chlorophyll absorbs primarily blue and red light.
The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 299792458 meters per second. It is a defined constant in SI units.
Mount Everest rises 8849 meters above sea level. It sits on the border of Nepal and China.
